quest:516.text: Beren's Peril. In southern Silverpine Forest, Shadow Priest Allister moves against Scourge gathering in a hidden cave. The Forsaken hope to strike before the undead begin their offensive. Shadow Priest Allister has heard that servants of the Lich King gather deep in southern Silverpine Forest. Their growing numbers threaten Forsaken operations across the region. So Allister sends scouts to strike first and destroy the Scourge in their secluded lair before they can mobilize. South of Ambermill, the Dalaran-aligned settlement, a hidden cave cuts into the hills. Its rough slopes make the cavern easy to miss, and the approach runs around the hills’ southern face. Ravenclaw drudgers and guardians dwell within. Destroying these Scourge remnants helps the Forsaken hold their ground in the forest.

quest:517.text: Elixir of Agony. In Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon puts his Elixir of Agony to a deadly test. He sends Horde champions to Dun Garok for a keg of Shindigger Stout. Apothecary Lydon serves the Royal Apothecary Society and Lady Sylvanas from Tarren Mill. He has gathered lethal ingredients across Hillsbrad and finished a new concoction. Frogs and stray dogs cannot test its strength. Lydon wants to see what it does to living adversaries. Lydon needs a quiet way to carry his experiment. South of Hillsbrad, Ironforge dwarves hold the fortified stronghold of Dun Garok. He sends Horde agents into its underground barracks and mess halls. There, they must slip past dwarven rifles and axes to steal a keg of Shindigger Stout.

quest:524.text: Elixir of Agony. In Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon prepares a deadly poison for a cruel test. He plans to disguise it as stolen dwarven ale and use it on human prisoners. Apothecary Lydon gathers foul ingredients across the Hillsbrad Foothills and steals dwarven ale from Dun Garok. The Royal Apothecary Society has charged him with making a deadly brew called Elixir of Agony. Once mixed, the poison waits inside a keg that appears to hold ordinary mountain stout.

quest:527.text: Battle of Hillsbrad. Across Hillsbrad, the Forsaken strike at the farms that feed the human town. High Executor Darthalia directs the attack from Tarren Mill under Varimathras's command. High Executor Darthalia directs the Forsaken campaign from Tarren Mill. Varimathras in the Undercity has ordered her to break the human resistance in Hillsbrad Foothills. So Darthalia targets the northern fields before attacking the defended town. Those farms feed the town. Disrupting them cuts provisions to the human militia and brings disorder to the homesteads. The Forsaken press the human defenders while the Royal Apothecary Society prepares a plague meant to destroy the living and the Scourge. Darthalia uses the fighting to hold the humans down until the plague is ready. Farmer Ray and Farmer Getz are among the landowners killed in these early attacks.

quest:528.text: Battle of Hillsbrad. In Hillsbrad, Forsaken forces press south after strikes on the northern farms. Horde operatives now hunt the peasants who fled to the orchards. Hillsbrad's human farms have come under attack, driving laborers south into the fields. After strikes on the northern farms, many flee to the orchards and pastures of Hillsbrad Fields. They hope to escape the advancing undead. High Executor Darthalia sees their flight as a chance to break the township's remaining labor force and morale. From Tarren Mill, High Executor Darthalia orders Horde forces to hunt the displaced laborers in the fields. The peasants have no protection. Their deaths choke Hillsbrad's food supply and weaken civilian resolve. For Darthalia and the Forsaken, each human killed tightens their hold over the surviving township and helps keep Lordaeron in Forsaken hands.

quest:529.text: Battle of Hillsbrad. At Hillsbrad, the Forsaken press their advance against the humans who resist them. High Executor Darthalia orders the smithy in Hillsbrad Fields destroyed, hoping to cut off the weapons arming the local people. In the Hillsbrad Foothills, the Forsaken face fiercer resistance than High Executor Darthalia expected. Rural humans refuse to scatter or yield to the Deathstalkers and soldiers sent from Tarren Mill. The Forsaken learn that the peasantry fight with more than pitchforks and scythes. In the fields, they are being armed for war. At the southwestern edge of Hillsbrad Fields, Blacksmith Verringtan and his apprentices forge blades and armor for the militia from raw ore. Darthalia sends an operative to kill Verringtan, butcher his apprentices, and seize their stockpiled iron. She aims to weaken the settlement's defenses and use the metal in the eventual assault on Southshore.

quest:530.text: A Husband's Revenge. In the Undercity, Raleigh Andrean sends you to hunt the man who murdered his wife. An engraved ring from Silverpine Forest stirs Raleigh Andrean's mortal memories. He recalls his close friend Valdred Moray, who murdered Raleigh's wife, Deliah. The Scourge's chill and undeath have dulled his grief and love. Yet his thirst for revenge remains, and you are sent to find Valdred.

quest:532.text: Battle of Hillsbrad. In Hillsbrad town, Forsaken forces strike to break human rule. High Executor Darthalia directs the assault from Tarren Mill. Hillsbrad’s human defenders hold to their authority despite heavy losses in the fields and among the patrols. High Executor Darthalia knows the peasants and militia rally behind the town’s leaders. So she sends Forsaken operatives into the Town Hall to kill Magistrate Burnside and five councilmen. Without them, the town loses its command. Darthalia seeks to break Hillsbrad’s civic life as well as its leadership. She orders operatives to burn the Hillsbrad Proclamation, a political document bound to the settlement’s charter and pride. They also seize the town registry from surviving Alliance loyalists. Its official records and citizen rolls give Undercity’s intelligence a detailed view of the local people.

quest:5321.text:
The Sleeper Has Awakened. Kerlonian Evershade struggles to stay awake on the road from Darkshore to Maestra's Post in Ashenvale. Newly roused from a long sleep, he carries the Horn of Awakening and needs help past furbolgs and cultists. Kerlonian Evershade is a Druid of the Claw, newly awakened from sleep in the barrows. For millennia, druids communed with wild spirits through the Emerald Dream. The Third War called them to wake, but centuries of hibernation left Kerlonian struggling to stay conscious.

He set out south from Darkshore to meet Liladris Moonriver in Ashenvale, yet exhaustion soon overtook him. Sudden naps leave him helpless in the wilds, so he relies on a brass Horn of Awakening and passing allies to keep moving. The road from Darkshore into Ashenvale is dangerous for Kerlonian. In Twilight Vale, corrupted Blackwood furbolgs stalk the road. Farther south in Ashenvale, members of the Dark Strand cult lie in ambush. Sleep may lay Kerlonian down wherever he stands, so you need to keep watch and rouse him with the horn.

quest:536.text: Down the Coast. Along Hillsbrad's coast, Lieutenant Farren Orinelle leaves Southshore's defense to passing adventurers. Sent from Stormwind, he would rather drink ale than patrol while Torn Fin murlocs gather along the Western Strand. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle left Stormwind's city guard for a post in Southshore. The port feels dreary to him, and the harbor's fishy odor is more than he can bear. So he spends his days drinking at the inn instead of patrolling the frontlines. Marshal Redpath has ordered him to protect Southshore from nearby dangers, but Orinelle hires passing sellswords to do the work. The Western Strand runs along the coast west of Southshore. Orinelle scoffs at the murlocs as overgrown fish, yet the Torn Fin tribe threatens coastal travel and local shipping. Its tidehunters and oracles gather in camps along the breakers. There, they ambush anyone who strays too far from town walls, so clearing the shoreline means facing them.

quest:539.text: Battle of Hillsbrad. At Azurelode Mine, Horde forces strike to cut iron shipments to Alliance armories. High Executor Darthalia has ordered Foreman Bonds and his crew killed. High Executor Darthalia marked Azurelode Mine as vital to human strength after the Horde seized the Hillsbrad Town Registry in earlier raids. The mine lies just south of Hillsbrad Fields. There, workers keep drawing rich iron ore for Alliance weaponsmiths and armories. If the mine stays open, Southshore can rearm and strengthen its garrisons, undoing Tarren Mill’s earlier victories. Darthalia orders Horde forces to kill Foreman Bonds, the human overseer, and a large part of his workforce. The attack reaches into the mine’s dark shafts to halt production. Southshore receives a clear warning: the Forsaken can strike its supply lines and isolated labor camps.

quest:540.text: Preserving Knowledge. In Southshore, Loremaster Dibbs sends you into the Ruins of Alterac to save books from the ogres who have settled there. One worn leather volume matters most: it holds The Arm of Gri'lek, a work of ancient troll lore. Loremaster Dibbs fears for the books left in the Ruins of Alterac, now home to ogres. You search for the tomes they have looted and recover what you can. Dibbs would climb into the mountains to search too, but fears old bones would not survive the journey. Among the tomes, Loremaster Dibbs most wants a worn leather book containing The Arm of Gri'lek. Dibbs is bent on learning its ancient troll lore. The Ruins of Alterac were the last known home of an intact copy.

quest:541.text: Battle of Hillsbrad. In Hillsbrad, the Forsaken's campaign now turns on Dun Garok. High Executor Darthalia sends Horde champions to break the dwarven garrison aiding local humans and kill its commander, Captain Ironhill. High Executor Darthalia has already pressed the human farmers and town militia across the foothills. Now she directs Tarren Mill's fury at Ironforge's troops. Dwarven soldiers have taken up arms for Southshore, strengthening the human presence in Lordaeron. Darthalia sees that bond as an obstacle. She means to show the Alliance that aid for the human survivors will bring devastation. Dun Garok clings to Thoradin's Wall in southeastern Hillsbrad. Disciplined mountaineers hold the fortified stronghold, joined by skilled riflemen and battle-hardened priests. Horde forces must break through those defenders and kill Captain Ironhill. His death breaks Ironforge's forward command in the region, leaving the remaining human enclaves isolated.

quest:5421.text: Fish in a Bucket. In Shadowprey Village, Jinar'Zillen leaves the shellfish gathering to others. The traps lie below the docks, and he offers a Bloodbelly fish for every five shellfish. Jinar'Zillen keeps many shellfish traps below the docks of Shadowprey Village. He would rather someone else gather from them, and offers a fine Bloodbelly fish for every five shellfish brought in.

quest:546.text: Souvenirs of Death. At Tarren Mill, Deathguard Samsa watches others march against Hillsbrad's human settlements and longs to join them. He asks for thirty human skulls taken in battle for his collection. High Executor Darthalia directs the Forsaken campaign against Hillsbrad's human settlements. Deathguard Samsa keeps watch in Tarren Mill while others are sent to raid, burn, and pillage. He envies their chance to slaughter the living, denied to a guard held at his post. Samsa hates the humans of Hillsbrad and collects the skulls of those slain in the campaign. He asks for thirty as trophies from a war he longs to fight himself. No arcane rite or military plan lies behind his request.

quest:547.text: Humbert's Sword. Near Dun Garok, Humbert's Sword is missing from the camp where its owner left it. Deathguard Humbert had gone for firewood while watching the dwarven stronghold on High Executor Darthalia's orders. Ironforge scouts took his weapon, and now he fears Darthalia will learn he failed. Deathguard Humbert watches Dun Garok for High Executor Darthalia. His hidden post lies near the dwarven fortress. One morning, he leaves camp to gather firewood for boiling water. Ironforge scouts find the post unguarded and loot it. When Humbert returns, his sword is gone, carried into the heavily defended bunker. Humbert knows losing his weapon to the enemy he was sent to watch could cost him his life under Forsaken command. If High Executor Darthalia learns what happened, he fears she will hang him from the rafters in Tarren Mill. He cannot storm Dun Garok alone. So he turns to passing Horde adventurers to recover his blade before his commander notices anything amiss.

quest:549.text: WANTED: Syndicate Personnel. At Tarren Mill, Lady Sylvanas Windrunner's bounty calls for every Syndicate member's death. The Forsaken want the brigands driven from Durnholde Keep before they threaten Horde operations in the foothills. The Syndicate's sudden arrival southeast of Tarren Mill has drawn the Forsaken's attention. Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and her commanders see the Syndicate as a plague, not displaced nobles to bargain with. Her bounty orders their immediate death. Any prisoners brought in will be executed without trial. Durnholde Keep was once an infamous internment fortress. Now it lies shattered and lawless. Syndicate Rogues and Watchmen have taken its crumbling ramparts and towers as an operations hub. High Executor Darthalia needs the armed bandits driven out to secure the road and protect Tarren Mill's southeastern approach.

quest:555.text: Soothing Turtle Bisque. Chef Jessen wants Soothing Turtle Bisque back on Southshore's tavern menu. Unrest has cut off his snapjaw turtle meat, so he asks cooks to brave the northern waters near Dalaran and Lake Lordamere. Southshore is one of Lordaeron's last intact coastal towns held by the Alliance. Civilian life continues there amid growing strife. Chef Jessen says his cooking rivals any tavern north of Stormwind. Patrons supposedly come from Darkshire in Duskwood to taste his bisque. The rich soup calls for fresh meat from snapjaw turtles native to the rivers and lakes of the northern mountains. In calmer years, Jessen gathered turtle meat himself. He traveled past Dalaran to the eastern shore of Lordamere Lake. Now rising tensions, hostile wildlife, the Syndicate, and Forsaken incursions make the lands beyond town deadly for ordinary townsfolk. To keep the bisque on his menu, Jessen relies on armed travelers to gather meat from snapjaws along the riverbanks and northern shores.

quest:56.text: The Night Watch. In Darkshire, The Night Watch holds the line against the dead rising nearby. Stormwind has withdrawn its garrison, leaving the town’s local militia to rely on travelers at Tranquil Gardens Cemetery. Stormwind once guarded Duskwood, but its royal resources dwindled as political discord took hold in the capital. Then the crown withdrew its commissioned soldiers, leaving Darkshire with little defense against the forest’s encroaching shadows. The people formed a local militia called the Night Watch, led by Commander Althea Ebonlocke. It stands between the cursed forest and the town’s remaining residents. South of Darkshire, Tranquil Gardens Cemetery was once a peaceful resting place. Now restless skeletons and reanimated spellcasters roam its graves. The Night Watch is stretched thin along Duskwood’s borders, so Commander Ebonlocke sends arriving travelers to strike down Skeletal Warriors and Skeletal Mages before the dead reach the roads.

quest:5643.text: Shadowguard. In the Undercity, Aelthalyste sends a Darkspear priest across the Great Sea to Orgrimmar. She has seen the young troll grow ready for the tribe’s sacred rites, and Ur'kyo awaits in the Valley of Spirits. In the Undercity, Aelthalyste watches the troll priests who come to learn. When an initiate grows strong enough for the tribe’s trials, she sends them across the Great Sea to their own elders. She does not press Forsaken teachings upon them. Their faith follows the traditions of their people. In Orgrimmar’s Valley of Spirits, Ur'kyo tends to the Darkspear tribe’s spiritual needs and ancient rites. He welcomes the returning initiate and prepares them for a rite of passage. The rite deepens the priest’s bond with the loa and uses spells to ward off harm.

quest:5644.text: Devouring Plague. Across the sea from Lordaeron, Devouring Plague awaits Forsaken priests ready to learn its dark art. Miles Welsh in Thunder Bluff sends the adept to Aelthalyste in the Ruins of Lordaeron for this signature Shadow magic. In Thunder Bluff, Miles Welsh trains Forsaken priests among the tauren. He watches their divine and shadowy studies, and knows when an acolyte is ready for higher mysteries. Rather than teach those secrets himself in Kalimdor, Miles sends the worthy back to the Ruins of Lordaeron. Aelthalyste waits beneath the city ruins in the Undercity's War Quarter. She is one of the foremost mentors of the Forsaken priesthood, guiding acolytes who weave shadow. Devouring Plague drains its victim and carries a corruptive force. Aelthalyste teaches it only to those able to wield that force without succumbing.

quest:5645.text: A Lack of Fear. In Ironforge, High Priest Rohan tests promising dwarven disciples. In the Mystic Ward, he teaches them as their strength of spirit grows. Local mentors send priests serving the Alliance abroad to senior clergy of their order. For dwarven disciples, that summons brings you to High Priest Rohan in Ironforge's Mystic Ward. There, basic spiritual practice gives way to deeper uses of holy magic, tested through trials. Dwarven tradition teaches that the Light is a shield in physical conflict. When you report to High Priest Rohan, you show that you have endured trials in the wider world. Now you must prove your mettle and master fear on the front lines.

quest:5646.text:
Devouring Plague. In Orgrimmar, Ur'kyo sends Forsaken priests home to learn Devouring Plague. They came to Kalimdor to learn from the Darkspear, but Aelthalyste waits in Undercity to teach them their people's shadow arts. Ur'kyo guides those drawn to spiritual power in Orgrimmar. Darkspear trolls and Forsaken share a curious bond in matters of faith, while orcs and tauren show little desire for priestly worship. Ur'kyo knows Forsaken initiates must master the shadow arts tied to their own condition. Out of respect between their peoples, he sends wandering Forsaken back to Lordaeron to finish their training. Beneath Lordaeron's ruins, Priestess Aelthalyste tends her flock in Undercity's War Quarter. Forsaken priests follow a solitary, grueling path shaped by their turn to shadow. They endure the painful touch of the Holy Light and learn to wield the devastating affliction of Shadow magic.

When an initiate gains enough skill, Aelthalyste gathers them close. There, she teaches the affliction her kind calls Devouring Plague.

quest:567.text: Dangerous!. At Tarren Mill, High Executor Darthalia names four Hillsbrad humans for execution. She says they killed Forsaken and struck at supplies. Across Hillsbrad Foothills, the fighting is brutal and personal. High Executor Darthalia and the Forsaken garrison at Tarren Mill see ordinary Hillsbrad citizens as deadly foes. A wanted notice names four people whose resistance has killed Forsaken and cost them valuable shipments from the Undercity. The bounty names Clerk Horrace Whitesteed, who killed Deathguard Toma; Citizen Wilkes, who murdered Apothecary Eli; Miner Hackett, who killed Deathstalker Fry; and Farmer Kalaba, who sabotaged supply convoys from the Undercity. Each works from a different pocket of Hillsbrad resistance and remains elusive amid the wider conflict.

quest:5672.text: Elune's Grace. In Darnassus, young night elf priests answer the Sisterhood of Elune's call. Their first journeys prepare them for deeper teaching from Priestess Alathea. In the Temple of the Moon, the Sisterhood guides young acolytes from their first prayers toward mastery of lunar magic. Night elves trust the Mother Moon, Elune. Humans and dwarves instead follow the Holy Light. When a novice reaches a milestone in devotion, senior mentors take notice and judge the disciple ready to bear greater divine power. Priestess Alathea brings the Sisterhood's summons to the acolyte. She honors their devotion and welcomes them into traditions kept through millennia. By accepting the rite, the novice seals a bond with Elune. From then on, protective wards and lunar invocations of the kaldorei faith are within reach.

quest:5674.text: Elune's Grace. Night elf priests leave Dolanaar for Darnassus to receive Elune's Grace. The rite marks their readiness for a divine talent reserved for the kaldorei. A priest of the Sisterhood of Elune needs more than skill in prayers of mending and smiting. With experience, an acolyte reaches the point where blessings reserved for the kaldorei may be bestowed. Local mentors such as Laurna Morninglight in Dolanaar cannot teach these deeper arts, so they send promising disciples to the spiritual heart of their order. Initiates cross Teldrassil to the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. There, beneath the gaze of the high priesthood, Priestess Alathea judges whether each petitioner is ready to bear the goddess's defensive mantle. She teaches Elune's Grace there, a divine talent reserved for the kaldorei.

quest:5676.text: Arcane Feedback. In Stormwind, High Priestess Laurena teaches Arcane Feedback to priests bound for dangerous roads. At the Cathedral of Light, faith becomes a defense against hostile spellcasters. At the Cathedral of Light, High Priestess Laurena warns the acolytes that arcane magic remains dangerous. The Holy Light brings healing, warmth, and divine order. Raw magic can turn volatile and lead to corruption or catastrophe. Warlocks, renegade sorcerers, and magical beasts threaten the faithful, so priests learn to make their faith an active ward against spells. Arcane Feedback turns a hostile spellcaster's power back against them. The ward does more than deflect spells; it burns through the caster's mana and brings agony. Laurena teaches the rite to human priests preparing to travel beyond Stormwind. Thus the Cathedral's emissaries can face sorcery with a defense of their own.

quest:5677.text: Arcane Feedback. In Ironforge, human acolytes seeking deeper teaching are sent back to Stormwind. There, the Cathedral of Light holds the traditions of their people. High Priest Rohan welcomes a human priest who seeks deeper spiritual teaching in Ironforge’s Mystic Ward. Dwarven and human priests both serve the Holy Light, yet each people keeps its own rites, disciplines, and prayers of defense. Rohan reserves Ironforge’s teachings for his own clergy. So he sends human priests back to Elwynn to learn the traditions of humankind. After reaching Stormwind City, the acolyte finds High Priestess Laurena in the Cathedral of Light. Laurena is relieved that Rohan’s guidance has brought the traveler to her, and welcomes them as their powers begin to grow. In the Cathedral, human priests can keep learning Stormwind’s spiritual practices. There they prepare to wield the Holy Light against the threats around the kingdom.

quest:5678.text: Arcane Feedback. Human priests are being called from Darnassus to Stormwind. At the Temple of the Moon, Priestess Alathea reluctantly honors the Alliance summons. High Priestess Laurena waits at the Cathedral of Light to prepare the acolyte for deeper instruction. Priestess Alathea oversees visiting priests at Darnassus's Temple of the Moon. She honors the formal alliance between the kaldorei and Stormwind, yet distrusts human ways of magic and faith. For ten millennia, grief from the War of the Ancients has shaped the night elves' fear of arcane power. Even human divine rites trouble the clergy when radiant faith blurs with arcane workings. Alathea honors the bond between the Alliance races and sends you to answer a recall from the Cathedral of Light. High Priestess Laurena has sent couriers across the seas to gather human priests for advanced training. In Stormwind, you leave Elune's moonlit groves for grand stone sanctuaries and the golden radiance of the Holy Light.

quest:5679.text: Devouring Plague. In the Undercity, Devouring Plague marks the shadow path of Forsaken priests. Priestess Aelthalyste teaches the rite to those who have proven their dedication to shadow magic. In the Undercity’s War Quarter, Priestess Aelthalyste teaches Forsaken priests the grim arts of the Shadow. Priests of other races draw on the Holy Light or ancestral spirits, while the Forsaken have shaped their own spiritual doctrines. Devouring Plague gives that path a fearsome form. It torments foes and drains their stolen vitality to sustain the caster’s decaying body. Priestess Aelthalyste shares the plague’s power with care. This potent weapon is meant to turn the tide against the Scourge and the Scarlet Crusade. She warns her disciples to practice until their command is sure. Greater trials await those who seek mastery of the dark arts.

quest:57.text: The Night Watch. Across Duskwood, restless dead rise from their graves, and The Night Watch struggles to hold them back. Commander Althea Ebonlocke sends travelers into the haunted barrows to defend Darkshire. Their fight may keep the town from falling to darkness. Duskwood’s graveyards stir beneath the forest’s twilight. Commander Althea Ebonlocke leads Darkshire’s volunteer militia, The Night Watch, against the rising dead. Stormwind sends no aid, and her forces are stretched thin. Skeletons and other horrors threaten the eastern settlements, so the militia calls on able travelers to enter the deadlands. Two places hold the militia’s attention: Tranquil Gardens Cemetery, just south of town, and Raven Hill Graveyard, far to the west. Skeletons rise from forgotten tombs and shallow graves beside the roads, stirred by dark magic in the forest’s shadows. Cutting them down gives Darkshire’s beleaguered citizens room to breathe. Yet the battle against this entrenched evil never ends.

quest:575.text: Supply and Demand. In Booty Bay, Drizzlik is preparing an order for Director Riddlevox, chief inventor of the Tinkers' Union. The leathercrafter claims to be the finest in the South Seas and beyond. Drizzlik calls his leatherwork exquisite and famed everywhere. Director Riddlevox has ordered twelve Excelsior-line boots, among Drizzlik's best sellers and the boots Riddlevox favors. To begin shaping them, Drizzlik needs skins from crocolisks by the northern Stranglethorn river. His equipment is ready, and leaving so important a customer unsatisfied would be a poor idea.

quest:5762.text: Hemet Nesingwary. A crate delayed on the road from Kalimdor reaches the jungles of Stranglethorn Vale by sea. At the Mirage Raceway, Kravel Koalbeard sends special supplies to Hemet Nesingwary, the renowned big-game hunter. At the Mirage Raceway in the Shimmering Flats, Kravel Koalbeard receives a long-overdue crate for one of his wealthy patrons. Hemet Nesingwary had already left Thousand Needles, but he paid to have the crate sent on to his hunting camp in Stranglethorn Vale. Kravel stays behind rather than face the arduous journey himself. So he hires passing adventurers to carry the crate across the sea. North of Grom'gol Base Camp, Hemet Nesingwary's expedition receives the heavy crate. It holds specialized heavy-gauge ammunition for bringing down the jungle's dangerous predators. Hemet recognizes the white salt crust on the courier's gear. His old dealings with Kravel have brought the firepower his safari needed.

quest:5763.text:
Hunting in Stranglethorn. You carry Roon Wildmane's token north of Grom'gol Base Camp to Hemet Nesingwary in Stranglethorn. The tauren and dwarf once hunted together in Desolace. Roon Wildmane remembers hunting beside Hemet, a dwarf who came to Desolace to hunt great beasts. Hemet wielded a rifle with uncanny skill. For many days, the two hunted together and set aside the old enmity between their peoples.

When Hemet left for Stranglethorn, Roon vowed to welcome him back for another hunt. Now Roon sends you with his kodo horn, a token Hemet will recognize. Find Hemet in Stranglethorn, north of Grom'gol Base Camp.

quest:58.text: The Night Watch. In eastern Raven Hill, The Night Watch sends for help as Darkshire faces the undead. Commander Althea Ebonlocke calls on travelers to enter the crypts and destroy the plague spreaders while her guards defend the town. This is the last chapter in the guard’s direct fight against the undead overrun. Darkshire stands nearly alone, with no soldiers from Stormwind to rely on. Its civilian militia, The Night Watch, must hold the town. Commander Althea Ebonlocke has few guards to spare, and she uses them to protect the crossroads, the town’s edge, and the supply lines. As the restless dead multiply across Duskwood, she calls on wandering champions to carry the fight into Raven Hill’s depths. The eastern mausoleum in Raven Hill Cemetery holds one of the region’s largest concentrations of undead. Unlike the open barrows, its stone crypts teem with plague spreaders. These ghouls carry afflictions that can sicken the living. Destroying twenty gives The Night Watch room to breathe and helps keep Darkshire from facing a united undead surge from the west.

quest:583.text: Welcome to the Jungle. In Stranglethorn Vale, Barnil Stonepot welcomes newcomers to the hunting camp and spots a seasoned wanderer. He offers to introduce you to Hemet Nesingwary, the expedition's leader. Barnil Stonepot greets newcomers at the camp in Stranglethorn Vale. He spots seasoned fighters and points out Hemet Nesingwary, an Alliance war hero and peerless tracker. Nesingwary keeps company with veterans who have proved themselves. Barnil thinks the old marksman may share his hunting wisdom with someone who has endured battle.

quest:5881.text: Calling in the Reserves. At Sun Rock Retreat, Maggran Earthbinder sends you south to relieve a weary sentry at the Great Lift. He gives you a letter for Grish Longrunner, who has stood watch far from home. Maggran Earthbinder keeps troop welfare and supplies in hand at Sun Rock Retreat in the Stonetalon Mountains. Across Kalimdor, the Horde strains to keep its garrisons staffed, even after the Third War. Maggran knows that endless watch duty wears seasoned soldiers down. So he sends a reassignment letter south to the Great Lift, where Grish Longrunner has stood guard far from home. The Great Lift joins the southern Barrens to the canyons of Thousand Needles. With Maggran's letter in hand, Grish can leave his lonely watch over the lift mechanisms and return to his family. Fresh reserves can take his place.

quest:6282.text: Harpies Threaten. In the Charred Vale, Bloodfury harpies threaten the roads west of Sun Rock Retreat. Maggran Earthbinder calls Horde warriors to thin their growing ranks and keep travel through Stonetalon open. Tauren at Sun Rock Retreat guard Stonetalon and its peaceful travelers. Maggran Earthbinder, the retreat’s elder leader, has watched the harpy ranks grow. The Bloodfury coven has spread through the scorched Charred Vale, harrying beasts and blocking routes. If the flocks grow further, Sun Rock Retreat could be cut off. West of Sun Rock Retreat, the Charred Vale is a wasteland of ash, scorched earth, and smoldering trees left by catastrophic fires. Bloodfury harpies nest high in the charred remains of ancient woods, and the vale is their stronghold. Maggran sends Horde warriors into the hostile caldera to cull dozens of harpies: Bloodfury ambushers, slayers, and roguefeathers. Thinning their ranks weakens the coven’s grip on the vale and clears the way to confront its matriarchal lineage.

quest:6283.text: Bloodfury Bloodline. Maggran Earthbinder sends you into the Charred Vale to break the harpies’ hold and bring back proof. Harpies from the edge of the Charred Vale threaten Sun Rock Retreat. Maggran Earthbinder believes their attacks will end only when Bloodfury Ripper, their matriarch, is dead. The flock treats her like a queen. Under her lead, they move as one and grow bold along the craggy western ridge. Maggran asks you to bring back Bloodfury Ripper’s remains as proof. Without their brood queen, the harpies lose their order and become easier to keep at bay. Sun Rock Retreat faces less danger, and Maggran can set aside his anger and constant watchfulness. Then he is free to seek the harmony and balance the tauren value.

quest:6284.text: Arachnophobia. A Horde bounty sends you west of Windshear Crag after Besseleth, the ancient spider haunting southern Stonetalon Mountains. Bring her fang to Maggran Earthbinder at Sun Rock Retreat, and travelers may find the mountain roads safer after dark. A weathered wanted poster warns travelers on the main road south of Windshear Crag to beware the lands west of it. Sishir Canyon and Webwinder Path swarm with spiders. Besseleth, an unusually large orange spider, commands her brood. After sunset, she ambushes anyone who strays from the path. Maggran Earthbinder, a tauren at Sun Rock Retreat, has posted the bounty on Besseleth. In an earlier encounter, her massive two-foot fang struck him and nearly killed him. Maggran fought her off and limped to safety, but the wound still reminds him of the danger in the canyon shadows. He hopes you will bring him Besseleth's Fang and secure the passes, so trade and travel to Sun Rock Retreat can continue without fear.

quest:63.text: Call of Water. Across the sea, Call of Water sends Barrens shamans to a blighted shore in Silverpine Forest. There, an initiate faces the sickness at an ancient shrine to earn communion with water spirits. You gather pure water with help from the hermit Brine, then return to Islen Waterseer on the Barrens coast. She sends you across the sea with the purified essence to Silverpine Forest's haunted shore. The shrine lies just west of the Forsaken refuge called the Sepulcher.

quest:6301.text: Cycle of Rebirth. At Sun Rock Retreat, Tammra Windfield seeks Gaea seeds to heal Stonetalon. She asks the Horde to gather them from Mirkfallon Lake, so she can bless them and restore the mountain’s damaged soil. Logging and clashes between rival factions have scarred Stonetalon’s peaks. Forests have been scorched, cut down, or reduced to ash. For the tauren at Sun Rock Retreat, the swift ruin of the natural world is a grievous wound. Shamans such as Tammra Windfield turn to the Earthmother’s renewing cycle as they work to mend the land. Tammra seeks rare Gaea seeds along Mirkfallon Lake, north of Sun Rock Retreat. Sturdy seed pods grow on the banks by the water, holding a resilience found only in Stonetalon. Once gathered, Tammra gives each kernel an ancestral shamanistic blessing. The blessing awakens its power and hastens its growth.

quest:631.text: The Thandol Span. At the Thandol Span, Rhag Garmason seeks a missing dwarf scout after a blast destroys the northern crossing. The Dark Iron clan has attacked Dun Modr, cutting off word and leaving its defenders without reinforcements. Ol' Rustlocke may know what caused the blast. A blast has torn through the bridge between Wetlands and the Arathi Highlands. Bronzebeard soldiers at the border were caught in the destruction when Dark Iron dwarves attacked Dun Modr. Their ranks are thin, and their strongholds are under siege. Longbraid the Grim leads the survivors as they hold their ground against the attackers. Longbraid sent veteran scout Ebenezer Rustlocke to inspect the eastern span. He was to learn whether a crossing or northern route remained usable. Days have passed without word from him. Dun Modr is under siege, and Rhag Garmason and the garrison have too few soldiers to search the enemy-held rubble.

quest:632.text: The Thandol Span. At the Thandol Span, Rhag Garmason waits for word from a missing scout. He sent adventurers to check on Ol' Ebenezer Rustlocke after the dwarf stopped reporting from the great stone crossing. The search beneath its arches may reveal a threat to northern supply lines. Longbraid the Grim sent Ebenezer Rustlocke to watch over the Thandol Span's structure and security. When the scout stopped reporting, foul play was feared.

quest:633.text: The Thandol Span. On the Thandol Span, a murder puts Ironforge’s northern road at risk. Ebenezer Rustlocke is dead, and Rhag Garmason has found explosives hidden by Kam Deepfury. A recovered document lays bare the crime beneath the Thandol Span. Ebenezer Rustlocke was murdered in the bridge’s substructure. The papers reveal more: Kam Deepfury, the Dark Iron agitator who first destroyed part of the bridge, has not stopped. His network planted another cache of heavy munitions just across the northern border in the Arathi Highlands, ready to finish the destruction.

quest:634.text: Plea To The Alliance. At the shattered Thandol Span, Plea To The Alliance carries Dun Modr's desperate call for aid. Dark Iron infiltrators slaughtered the garrison, and its dwarven survivors appeal to human forces at Refuge Pointe, though the Alliance is stretched thin. Dun Modr lies in ruins, and Dark Iron dwarves have sabotaged the Thandol Span. The survivors cling to a foothold on the Wetlands' northern rim. Ironforge's main reserves have not arrived, so Rhag Garmason and Longbraid the Grim look north to the Arathi Highlands. There they learn that Alliance forces have camped at Refuge Pointe. Garmason sends an emissary across the shattered bridge to ask Captain Nials for urgent military aid. At Refuge Pointe, Captain Nials offers sympathy to Longbraid's soldiers but cannot spare a single fighter. Stromgarde has fallen into ruin, overrun by Syndicate rogues, Boulderfist ogres and Witherbark trolls. Its surviving defenders are committed to reclaiming their ancestral capital. Bound by honor and pressed by their own desperate struggle, Nials sends word that the dwarves at the Span must stand alone.

quest:637.text: Sully Balloo's Letter. At the Thandol Span, Sully Balloo's Letter carries a dwarf's last words to his wife in Ironforge. Found beneath the bridge, it tells where he died. Beneath the stone pilings of the Thandol Span, the land bridge between the Wetlands and the Arathi Highlands, a drowned skeleton still clutches an envelope. Its water-damaged pages begin, “My dear Sara,” and preserve the tenderness of Sully Balloo's careful writing. Alliance forces and their enemies have fought fiercely for the Thandol Span. Dark Iron saboteurs and warbands contesting the borderlands have threatened the crossing. Sully Balloo was among the dwarven soldiers sent north to defend it. His family in the mountains knew nothing of his fate until a diver brought his farewell letter up from beneath the waves.

quest:6381.text: New Life. Tammra Windfield sends travelers west from Sun Rock Retreat to begin healing the Charred Vale. She hopes Gaea seeds can help the scorched land recover. Tammra Windfield asks you to enter the Charred Vale, where soot, fire elementals, and harpies haunt the ruined ground. She trusts the Earth Mother's resilience. Find the Gaea Dirt Mounds, where fertile soil survived the fire. Gaea seeds can take root despite the lingering elemental corruption. Their roots hold back decay and give plants a place to return to the valley. Tammra hopes new growth will calm the fire spirits and drive the harpies from their desolate roost. She also hopes the Venture Company's logging will eventually be driven out.

quest:6382.text: The Ashenvale Hunt. In Ashenvale, the Horde's proven hunters face a new test beneath ancient trees. Jorn Skyseer sends you north from Camp Taurajo to Splintertree Post, where Senani Thunderheart awaits. After proving yourself in the Barrens, you are sent toward Ashenvale. Jorn Skyseer sees when a hunter has outgrown the local game and points the way north. For the young Horde, these old forests offer resources and mark a political and spiritual frontier to understand and claim. The road north passes the Mor'shan Rampart before reaching Splintertree Post, a fortified Horde camp deep among the trees. Senani Thunderheart, a tauren huntress, welcomes experienced hunters seeking harder tests of survival. The Horde needs skilled trackers to face Ashenvale's native predators and the forest's watchful defenders.

quest:6383.text: The Ashenvale Hunt. In Ashenvale, Horde hunters face three great predators in Senani Thunderheart's trial at Splintertree Post. Track Ursangous, Shadumbra, and Sharptalon to prove your skill. Senani Thunderheart gives the Horde's presence in Ashenvale a different kind of test. While Orcs gather lumber, she sends hunters into the shadowed forest to face its strongest predators. Strength alone will not serve; hunters need cunning and respect for the wilderness. They must learn what they can endure. Three solitary beasts test those who take up the hunt. Ursangous, an immense elder bear, roams near the Talondeep Path. Shadumbra, a cunning nightsaber, stalks the eastern borders near Raynewood Retreat and the Laughing Sisters. South of Splintertree Post, Sharptalon, a fierce hippogryph, wheels above the forest canopy.

quest:6393.text: Elemental War. In Stonetalon Mountains, Tsunaman sends you against fire elementals in Neptulon’s name. The water envoy at Sun Rock Retreat asks you to enter the Charred Vale and gather Incendrite cores from the blazing elementals you destroy. Their struggle reaches beyond mortal borders, bound to the ancient rivalry between elemental forces. At Sun Rock Retreat in Stonetalon Mountains, Tsunaman speaks for the Tribunal of the Tides. You carry out Neptulon the Tidehunter’s will against the fiery kin of his water elementals. Their enmity reaches far beyond mortal borders. It is an ancient struggle between the primal forces of Azeroth. Southern Stonetalon Mountains hold the Charred Vale, where ash and smoke mark the land. Fire elementals gather there and threaten the surrounding regions. Tsunaman sends you to destroy them and gather the Incendrites they leave behind. These blazing cores prove to the Tribunal that the elementals are gone.

quest:647.text: MacKreel's Moonshine. Foggy MacKreel needs his moonshine carried from the broken Thandol Span to Southshore. He drank too much while on watch and now has little time to deliver a fresh batch to Brewmeister Bilger and settle his debt. On the shattered Thandol Span, Foggy MacKreel keeps watch through wet, cold, and dull hours. He drinks his homemade moonshine to bear the damp chill. The brew hits hard enough that he compares its aftereffects to siege engines pounding across his skull. One drink too many leaves him asleep through his shift. Longbraid the Grim commands the dwarves defending the Span, and Foggy cannot afford another lapse in discipline. Foggy owes Brewmeister Bilger in Southshore a longstanding debt. He promised a batch of his personal brew to settle the account, but his hangover and watch duties have left him minutes from missing the deadline. You race across the Arathi Highlands with the jug, by gryphon and swift feet. Reach Southshore before Bilger decides Foggy has skipped out on his tab again.

quest:6481.text: Earthen Arise. In Boulderslide Ravine, Mor'rogal finds Goggeroc asleep inside a Resonite cask. The tauren shaman fears the ancient Earthen could threaten all Kalimdor, so he sends a champion to break the cask and slay Goggeroc before its strength returns. Scouts searching Boulderslide Ravine for vermin found a strange relic among the kobolds. A Resonite cask held unearthly force. Mor'rogal, a tauren shaman in the Stonetalon Mountains, knew it was both prison and sanctuary for Goggeroc, a dormant Earthen. These ancient beings of stone can outmatch mortal warriors, and Goggeroc's freedom could endanger the whole region.

quest:6503.text:
Ashenvale Outrunners. In Ashenvale, Kuray'bin sends the Horde against night elf scouts slipping out from Silverwing Outpost. They are gathering word of Horde encampments and defenses before they can report back. Night elf scouts from Silverwing Outpost move through the woods east of their base and south of nearby Horde holdings. They watch the paths and ridges, mapping fortifications and tracking troop movements.

Kuray'bin has learned that these scouts, called Ashenvale Outrunners, have slipped into the wilderness to gather intelligence. The Horde strikes at enemy scouts before they can return to Silverwing Outpost. Hunting down the outrunners keeps their commanders from learning the Horde's troop strength and outpost defenses.

Without their forward eyes, the night elves are disoriented and less willing to risk aggressive moves through the contested woods.

quest:6504.text: The Lost Pages. A gust has scattered The Lost Pages across Ashenvale, leaving Gurda Ragescar stranded near Splintertree Post. She cannot run the shredder she is carrying from Ratchet to the Warsong Lumber Camp without its manual. The Warsong Clan buys steam-powered shredders in Ratchet to clear lumber across Ashenvale. Their delicate workings can be hard for an orc warrior to master. As Gurda Ragescar carried a newly bought shredder north, a sudden gust tore the instruction booklet from her hands. Twelve parchment leaves scattered across the forest floor. The wind carried the manual pages across Ashenvale. Wandering creatures, cultists, and forest denizens have taken them. The shredder cannot run without all three chapters. Gurda is stranded on the road to Splintertree Post, unable to report for logging duty.

quest:6546.text: Warsong Outrider Update. Along eastern Ashenvale, the Warsong Outrider Update carries word of danger closing in on the Horde. Its report names Alliance forces, satyr entrenched in the forest, and naga moving through neighboring Azshara. A lone Warsong Outrider watches Ashenvale’s contested eastern edge. Horde supply lines face constant harassment, so outriders track enemy movements before raiding parties can strike Mor'shan Rampart or Splintertree Post. Meet one on patrol and you know the forest is under watch. His report may decide whether a Horde fortification holds or falls to ambush. A Warsong Outrider’s report tells of danger across Kalimdor’s central forests. Night elves and the wider Alliance remain a threat, while cunning, demonic satyr haunt eastern Ashenvale. Scouts have also found a massive naga presence spreading through the ruined coastal lands of neighboring Azshara. The Horde faces hostile powers from nearly every direction.

quest:6547.text: Warsong Scout Update. Kadrak's orders reach Warsong Scout Update as scouts watch the contested woods. The Horde relies on their reports to guard its positions in Ashenvale from night elf attacks. Kadrak relies on scattered Warsong scouts to watch Ashenvale's border. Night elf sentinels use the forest for cover, and the scouts risk being cut off. Couriers carry written updates between them, keeping isolated outposts connected to Horde command and able to report what they see. Warsong scouts watch for night elf raids meant to reclaim the forest. The clan has paid in lives for every stretch of Ashenvale it cleared or occupied. Kadrak's orders keep forward scouts in touch with the Horde and let them report whether their defenses are holding against elven resistance.

quest:6561.text: Blackfathom Villainy. In Blackfathom Deeps, a wounded scout calls for help against the cult serving Aku'mai. Argent Dawn scout Thaelrid asks passing Horde champions to end Twilight Lord Kelris's blood sacrifices in the sunken ruins. Argent Dawn scout Thaelrid lies wounded in the underground temple along the Ashenvale coast. His reconnaissance uncovered horrors beyond the naga incursions, but he has spent his strength and cannot finish his mission alone. So he calls on passing Horde champions to strike at the cult's leaders in the sunken halls. Twilight Lord Kelris leads the Twilight's Hammer cultists in the ruined Temple of the Moon. Alongside the local naga, he performs dark rites over the defiled Moon Well. Captives are fed alive to Aku'mai, a ravenous hydra and beast of the Old Gods. Kelris seeks cosmic power and primordial chaos.

quest:6562.text:
Trouble in the Deeps. From Stonetalon Mountains, Tsunaman sends Horde travelers to aid Je'neu Sancrea on Ashenvale's remote coast. The troll scholar waits at Zoram'gar Outpost, where danger gathers along the shore. Tsunaman hears troubling reports from the north and calls Horde travelers to aid Je'neu Sancrea. The troll scholar waits at Zoram'gar Outpost on Ashenvale's far western shore, along the Zoram Strand. Danger is growing there, and Je'neu needs help from beyond the outpost. The road to Ashenvale's western shore is dangerous for Horde travelers. You can pass through Windshear Crag, where goblins have stirred trouble, or travel north from the Barrens. Either way, you enter a forest watched by night elf sentinels.

Far beneath Ashenvale's dense canopy, Zoram'gar Outpost holds on along the storm-washed Zoram Strand. The outpost faces the shadowed waters.

quest:6563.text: The Essence of Aku'Mai. At Zoram'gar Outpost, Je'neu Sancrea asks Horde adventurers to stop the naga's sapphire harvest in Blackfathom Deeps. He fears they will misuse the gems' power. From the Zoram Strand, Je'neu Sancrea watches over the Kaldorei ruins. Naga now mine sapphire clusters in the submerged chambers of Blackfathom Deeps, where the gems grow along damp cavern walls. Sancrea senses the serpentine invaders mean to harness their power, so he seeks to stop the harvest before they can use it. The Sapphires of Aku'mai carry elemental water energy and hold clinging water spirits. Adept sorcerers could fuel dangerous arcane rituals with them or strengthen Aku'mai, the shadowy hydra whose presence fills the subterranean temple. Recovering the clusters keeps this potent reagent from the naga and helps guard the coastline against unchecked elemental magic.

quest:6564.text: Allegiance to the Old Gods. At Zoram'gar Outpost, you bring Je'neu Sancrea a naga message from Blackfathom Deeps. Its orders point to a ritual plot in the flooded ruins. Horde scouts find a damp, crumpled note while fighting the naga in Blackfathom Deeps. Its frantic words order naga priestesses to gather elemental water crystals. These crystals are meant to fuel the summonings of naga aquamancers. The aquamancers are gathering elemental forces for a darker purpose.

quest:6565.text: Allegiance to the Old Gods. At Zoram'gar, the Horde moves against the Twilight's Hammer cult in Blackfathom Deeps. Je'neu Sancrea sends champions after Lorgus Jett, hoping to disrupt cultists who seek to awaken ancient forces of destruction beneath Ashenvale's coast. From the Ashenvale shore, Zoram'gar Outpost watches Blackfathom Deeps. Naga, corrupted beasts, and Twilight's Hammer fanatics overrun its submerged temple complex. Je'neu Sancrea is an Earthen Ring seer stationed on the coast. He sees the cultists serving the Old Gods rather than the land's natural balance and spirits. These monstrous beings of chaos were defeated in ancient times, yet their malign touch lingers in Azeroth's forgotten places. Je'neu sends Horde champions into the underground ruins to hunt Lorgus Jett, an established leader among the cultists in Blackfathom Deeps. Lorgus works deep in the stone passages between Ghamoo-ra's chamber and Baron Aquanis's chamber. Je'neu is too frail to enter the damp darkness himself. Lorgus's defeat is vital to severing the dark rituals he sought to orchestrate beneath Ashenvale's waves.

quest:6571.text: Warsong Supplies. At Splintertree Post, Locke Okarr needs Warsong Supplies to keep the lumber camp working. Some wait in town, some in Booty Bay, and others lie in enemy hands across Ashenvale. From Splintertree Post, Locke Okarr works to keep the Warsong Lumber Camp supplied. The Warsong Clan needs a steady flow of heavy tools to harvest Ashenvale's ancient timber. Furbolg and satyr raids have scattered or seized local supplies, leaving the camp short of vital gear. You gather equipment from across Kalimdor and beyond. Pixel, the goblin courier at Splintertree Post, has circular saw blades. In Booty Bay, Wharfmaster Lozgil holds a crate of heavy axes. Foulweald and Thistlefur furbolgs have taken logging ropes, while satyrs at Night Run, Satyrnaar, and Xavian stole barrels of Warsong machinery oil for their profane rites.

quest:6581.text: Warsong Saw Blades. At Splintertree Post, the Warsong loggers wait for blades brought from Ratchet. Their courier Pixel will trade the shipment for a weapon to guard herself on Ashenvale's dangerous roads. The blades keep the Horde's lumber camps at work. Pixel has brought heavy saw blades from Ratchet to Splintertree Post, but she will not give them away. In Ashenvale's wilds, safety matters more to her than coin. She asks to trade them for a Deadly Blunderbuss, so she can defend herself on the dangerous roads through hostile territory. The Horde needs Ashenvale timber to ease shortages across Durotar and the Barrens. Axes dull quickly against the ancient groves, so the Warsong loggers rely on goblin-forged blades. Pixel's shipment supplies the lumber camps, where the Horde cuts timber for outposts and war machines despite fierce resistance from the night elves.

quest:66.text: The Legend of Stalvan. Madame Eva's vision in Darkshire names Stalvan and warns of death for her granddaughter, Alyssa. She sends you to the Darkshire Town Hall to search the records. In Darkshire, Madame Eva reads cards and portents for troubled locals. A terrible disturbance jolts her awake, and she draws the Death card for her young granddaughter, Alyssa. Eva enters a deep trance to learn what the omen means. One clue comes to her: the name Stalvan. Fearing for her family and the town, she asks you to follow that name before tragedy strikes. Madame Eva sends you across the square to the Darkshire Town Hall. Search its records for Stalvan, and speak with Clerk Daltry, who keeps the town's ledgers and public archives. He can help determine whether Stalvan once lived in Darkshire, passed through as a traveler, or belongs to Duskwood's past.

quest:6621.text: King of the Foulweald. At Zoram'gar Outpost, Karang Amakkar orders a strike against the Foulweald. Horde champions plant a war banner on the tribe’s sacred totem mound, drawing out Chief Murgut and killing him. Karang Amakkar sees the corrupted Foulweald as a danger to the Horde from his post at Zoram'gar Outpost. The tribe is smaller than the northern Thistlefur, but its members are fierce. So Karang orders a show of force to break their will before they can ambush Horde patrols. Greenpaw Village lies northeast of Mystral Lake. Karang prepares a tribal war banner for the center of the Foulweald totem mound, insulting the tribe’s ancestral spirits and pride. The defenders rush to tear it down, and Chief Murgut emerges to defend his honor in open combat. Taking his personal totem breaks the tribe’s leadership and establishes Horde supremacy in the area.

quest:6627.text: Test of Lore. At Braug Dimspirit’s perch in Stonetalon, you face a test of ancient history. Having retrieved the tome Legacy of the Aspects, you must show what its lessons taught you. A wrong answer sends you far across Kalimdor. Braug Dimspirit’s trial follows the tests Dorn Plainstalker began at the Weathered Nook. It calls for understanding, not martial survival or blind trust. Braug lives among the crags of the Stonetalon Mountains. He expects seekers to recover ancient texts and learn from their pages. The lesson concerns how the Dragon Aspects were created and divided, and the pact they made long before the Great Sundering. Braug asks what the tome says about the Earth Warder, Neltharion. His madness and betrayal reshaped Azeroth’s surface. You must understand this history before continuing along the path of wisdom.

quest:6628.text: Test of Lore. In the Undercity, initiates face a test of history with Parqual Fintallas. They have scoured the world for historical texts, and this examination is part of spiritual trials begun in Thousand Needles. The Test of Lore is one of the spiritual trials begun in Thousand Needles. Dorn Plainstalker set the trials at the Weathered Nook. This examination carries candidates from the wind-carved canyons of Thousand Needles to the Undercity, where Parqual Fintallas tests their knowledge of history and holds each seeker to a high standard.

quest:67.text: The Legend of Stalvan. In Darkshire, Clerk Daltry searches the town records for Stalvan Mistmantle. An old address points west to Moonbrook in Westfall, where the search for Stalvan’s past begins. After your inquiries in Darkshire, Clerk Daltry searches the town registry for Stalvan Mistmantle. The ledger has gone years without an update, and lists Stalvan’s last known home as the schoolhouse in Moonbrook, far to the west. Daltry takes the old address as routine record keeping. He asks you to investigate and bring back any records that could bring Darkshire’s archives up to date. The trail runs from Duskwood into Westfall, where the Defias Brotherhood holds Moonbrook. Once a thriving farming settlement, the town is now under outlaw control. Near its center stands the abandoned schoolhouse. Inside, an old footlocker holds the first clear clues to Stalvan’s former life as an educator. A sorrow still lingers around the chest.

quest:68.text: The Legend of Stalvan. In Moonbrook, The Legend of Stalvan leads you back to Darkshire's records. A dusty, unsent letter from an old footlocker proves Stalvan Mistmantle stayed there before his trail went cold. You find a dusty, unsent letter in an old footlocker while tracing Stalvan Mistmantle's past. Moonbrook was once an agricultural settlement, but now lies in ruin, crowded with outlaws and restless specters. Few remember his brief stay, yet the letter places him in the hamlet. You carry the letter across the border to Darkshire, where Clerk Daltry keeps the town records. He finds it strange that the letter was never mailed, but the evidence confirms Stalvan's connection to Moonbrook. The records can now point toward where Stalvan fled next.

quest:681.text: Northfold Manor. At Refuge Pointe, Captain Nials seeks your help against the Syndicate at Northfold Manor. Their hold between Stromgarde's defenders and Southshore slows supplies. Ogres, the Syndicate and the Alliance divide Stromgarde, and the factions fight to a bloody stalemate. The Alliance's forces dwindle as their enemies grow. The defenders need help from Southshore, but supplies arrive slowly. The Syndicate holds the ground between the defenders and Southshore. Captain Nials asks you to go to Northfold Manor, the Syndicate's base, and cut down their highwaymen and mercenaries. He hopes easing their pressure will let more supply trains through.

quest:683.text: Sara Balloo's Plea. In Ironforge, Sara Balloo grieves for Sully and asks you to carry her plea to King Magni Bronzebeard. Sara has received Sully’s final letter, recovered from the waters of the Thandol Span. She wants the king to remember his sacrifice, so she writes him a plea. Grief keeps her from appearing before the throne herself. She entrusts the sealed letter to you, a champion of the Alliance, to carry to King Magni Bronzebeard.

quest:686.text: A King's Tribute. King Magni Bronzebeard answers Sara Balloo with a lasting tribute to her fallen husband, Sully. He sends you across Ironforge with a royal commission for Grand Mason Marblesten. Sara Balloo's plea weighs on King Magni Bronzebeard. War's harsh needs can be hard for common folk to understand, yet every soldier beneath the Alliance banner weighs on his conscience. He cannot undo a death on the front lines. He can see that Sully Balloo's sacrifice is remembered. King Magni chooses a stone memorial for Sully, not empty words. He entrusts you with his royal commission and sends you across Ironforge to Grand Mason Marblesten. The master stonemason receives the king's personal charge and prepares to carve the fallen defender's memory into stone.

quest:689.text: A King's Tribute. King Magni Bronzebeard has ordered a memorial for Sully Balloo, who died defending the Thandol Span. Grand Mason Marblesten sends you north to Hillsbrad for stone worthy of the fallen soldier. Grand Mason Marblesten carries King Magni Bronzebeard’s commission to honor Sully Balloo. Sully died in the disaster at the Thandol Span. Dark Iron saboteurs have attacked the span, a vital artery between the dwarven lands and the northern kingdoms. Marblesten will shape a sculpture to withstand time and war, so the Great Forge remembers the dwarven sacrifice. For Sully Balloo’s likeness, Marblesten requires Alterac Granite. Its dense, resilient stone and clean texture make it prized by masons. The finest deposits lie around Darrow Hill in Hillsbrad’s contested foothills. The journey into the troubled north is dangerous, but Marblesten seeks stone worthy of the heroism it will honor.

quest:69.text: The Legend of Stalvan. In Darkshire, a scratched registry entry sends the search for Stalvan Mistmantle toward Goldshire. Clerk Daltry finds another destination beneath Stalvan Mistmantle's earlier entry in Darkshire's town registry. The hurried note is partly scratched out. Someone meant to hide the route or changed their mind. It points northwest toward the Lion's Pride Inn in Elwynn Forest. You leave Duskwood's shadowed groves for Goldshire's sunny roads, where Stalvan's trail reaches too. The Lion's Pride Inn stands at Elwynn Forest's crossroads, where travelers, merchants, and soldiers gather. Innkeeper Farley runs the busy taproom and may know of an educated wanderer looking for a room.

quest:6921.text: Amongst the Ruins. At Zoram'gar Outpost, Je'neu Sancrea sends Horde champions beneath the waters of Blackfathom Deeps. The Earthen Ring hopes a fathom core will show what the Twilight's Hammer is doing to the elements. The Twilight's Hammer has seized Blackfathom Deeps, an ancient night elven temple once sacred to Elune. Its cultists now command the submerged passages. At Zoram'gar Outpost on Ashenvale's shore, Darkspear shaman Je'neu Sancrea watches the corruption spread. He fears the cult will turn the local elements against the land and its defenders. Je'neu Sancrea sends Horde champions to recover a fathom core from the fathom stone beneath the waters of the Moonshrine Ruins. Shamans who can read the core will find a detailed record of elemental currents and disturbances. The Earthen Ring hopes that record will reveal the Twilight's Hammer's work and help guard the region against elemental disaster.

quest:6922.text: Baron Aquanis. Beneath Ashenvale, Baron Aquanis leaves a strange globe filled with tainted fluid. Je'neu Sancrea of the Earthen Ring suspects the Twilight's Hammer cultists in the submerged ruins and hopes the globe will reveal what corrupted the elemental. In Blackfathom Deeps, foul sorcery has twisted Baron Aquanis into a water spirit. When the elemental is destroyed, a Strange Water Globe remains. The impervious orb holds putrid fluid that seems to have sustained and warped Aquanis's natural essence. Physical force cannot harm it. Its energies unsettle those attuned to the balance of the elements.

quest:6981.text: The Glowing Shard. Deep in the Wailing Caverns, you find a green shard whose smoky depths stir unease. Its mystery draws you to Ratchet and onward. You carry a green crystal from deep within the Wailing Caverns. Beneath its bright, solid face, shadowy wisps seem to churn. Those who touch it feel uneasy, and its strange presence hints at the corruption around the sleeping druids and their nightmare-haunted sanctuary.

quest:70.text: The Legend of Stalvan. In Goldshire, an old letter renews the search for Stalvan Mistmantle. Its trail runs from Elwynn Forest to Stormwind's Canal District. At the Lion's Pride Inn, Innkeeper Farley recalls a stormy night years ago. A traveling courier came in from the rain to find shelter. Around midnight, he rushed downstairs in a panic, wearing only his sleepwear. He vanished into the storm, and no one saw him again. The courier left his satchel and personal chest in the upstairs room. Among the forgotten cargo was an unsent letter bearing the name Stalvan, addressed to someone in Stormwind City's Canal District. The chest remained untouched at the foot of the bed until Farley allowed it to be opened.

quest:700.text: A King's Tribute. Magni Bronzebeard gives Sully Balloo a memorial in Ironforge. Granite from Lordaeron keeps the fallen dwarf in his people's memory. King Magni Bronzebeard commissioned a monument for Sully Balloo, a dwarf who died serving his people. Grand Mason Marblesten carved it from fine granite brought from Lordaeron's war-torn lands. The monument stands in Ironforge, honoring soldiers whose sacrifices help preserve the dwarven kingdom. When told the monument is complete, Magni considers stone and mortality. Carved rock can never equal a brave dwarf's life, he knows, yet he hopes the memorial endures. Then generations walking Azeroth may remember the heroes who bled to secure their tomorrow.

quest:72.text: The Legend of Stalvan. In Stormwind, you search for Stalvan Mistmantle among the Flintridge belongings. By the canals, sealed crates hold what remains of the household, watched over by restless spirits tied to the massacre. You follow Stalvan’s path from Duskwood to Stormwind. Beside the city canals, Caretaker Folsom guards what remains of the Flintridge household. His father served the estate before him and had to mop up blood after a massacre claimed the household. Somehow, Stalvan’s name is tied to that slaughter. The Flintridge trust funds are gone, and royal tax collectors press the estate. Surviving heirlooms and packed belongings wait inside sealed shipping crates along the canal embankment, awaiting auction. You search them for Stalvan’s trail before the family’s remaining goods scatter to collectors across the kingdom.

quest:729.text: The Absent Minded Prospector. In southern Darkshore, hostile stone golems overrun a dig site, and Archaeologist Hollee seeks help in Auberdine. She fears for Prospector Remtravel, her senior colleague, whose research often blinds him to mortal danger. Archaeologist Hollee came across the sea with the Explorers' League. Master Greywhisker sent her to apprentice under Prospector Remtravel, whose discoveries had made him renowned in Ironforge's academic circles. The League sent them to study ancient ruins along Darkshore's untamed coast. As they dug through what seemed to be the remains of a great civilization, violent stone golems burst from the earth and overran the site. In panic, Hollee fled through the night to Auberdine, the night elf port, to seek help. Remtravel barely noticed the danger. Absorbed in his relics, the elderly prospector stayed among the rubble as lumbering constructs surrounded his camp. South of Auberdine, anyone who reaches him finds him grumbling about missing stone brushes and misplaced fossils.

quest:731.text: The Absent Minded Prospector. At Darkshore's southern ruins, Prospector Remtravel presses on with his dig, hoping to find a prize for the Explorers' League. Hostile troggs and his forgetfulness make the search perilous, and word of his safety must reach his assistant in Auberdine. Far south in Darkshore, Remtravel's Dig lies among ancient ruins. Dwarven excavators searching there uncovered troggs, who drove out the workers and besieged their camp. Remtravel will not return to Auberdine empty-handed. He wanders into danger to recover a fossil, hoping to justify the expedition's costs to the Explorers' League.

quest:7321.text: Soothing Turtle Bisque. In Tarren Mill, Christoph Jeffcoat hopes Soothing Turtle Bisque will prove the Forsaken can cook with care. He needs snapjaw meat from Hillsbrad's waterways and the shores of Lordamere Lake. Many think the Forsaken have given up the comforts of life, fine cooking among them. Christoph Jeffcoat in Tarren Mill holds otherwise. He boasts that his rich turtle bisque could tempt souls back from beyond the grave. With care in the cooking, he means to show that undead hands can still make a warming dish in a land marked by plague and war. Jeffcoat once gathered ingredients from Hillsbrad's waterways and Lordamere Lake's eastern shores in neighboring Alterac. Now his duties in Tarren Mill and nearby Alliance forces keep him from hunting. So he relies on passing Horde cooks to hunt snapjaws and bring back their meat. Their help keeps his recipe alive.

quest:74.text: The Legend of Stalvan. Beside Stormwind City's canals, you find a clue to Stalvan Mistmantle's past in the Flintridge crate. Its torn journal page points toward Marshal Haggard in Elwynn Forest. Beneath a ceramic vase in the sealed crate lies a torn page from Stalvan Mistmantle's journal. Musty Flintridge heirlooms, old hunting trophies, and family portraits fill the crate. Stalvan's own hand offers a glimpse of the reclusive scholar before tragedy struck.

quest:741.text: The Absent Minded Prospector. From Darkshore, Hollee sends Remtravel’s fossil to Darnassus while she stays to watch the wandering prospector. Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker takes a keen interest in the find. Prospector Remtravel has found a curious fossil on Darkshore’s coast. He would rather keep digging than follow protocol. So Archaeologist Hollee stays with him among the shore’s dangerous beasts and hostile cultists. She asks you to carry the specimen to Darnassus, where a dwarven scholarly delegation is kept. Dwarves from Ironforge have crossed the Great Sea under the Explorers’ League banner. They seek ancient relics and lost history in Kalimdor’s soil. In Darnassus, Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker marvels at Remtravel’s knack for finding ancient treasures. Night elves see their forests as living sanctuaries, while the League sees ancient lands as ground to study and decipher.

quest:742.text: The Ashenvale Hunt. In Thunder Bluff, The Ashenvale Hunt sends young Horde champions north to serve at the forest outposts. Heralds direct them to report to Senani Thunderheart at Splintertree Post for a proving hunt. Bluff Runner Windstrider carries an open invitation through Thunder Bluff for proven adventurers. North of the Barrens, the Horde has footholds in an ancient forest, and its outposts need young warriors. Those who answer will face harsher country and test their survival skills beyond Mulgore. Ashenvale offers the Horde rich resources and severe peril. Splintertree Post lies along the main road, while a remote outpost stands on the western coast at Zoram Strand. At Splintertree Post, Senani Thunderheart is a veteran outdoorswoman who organizes a great hunt. There, recruits tame the wilderness and win glory for the Horde.

quest:75.text: The Legend of Stalvan. In Elwynn, your search for The Legend of Stalvan leads you to Marshal Haggard's home. The veteran's failing eyesight left an upstairs chest of papers unread. Marshal Haggard lives near Elwynn Forest's southeastern edge, close to Duskwood and Redridge. Upstairs, an old chest holds parchments he found when he moved into his secluded home. His failing eyesight kept him from reading them, and they have remained untouched until you ask about Stalvan.

quest:78.text: The Legend of Stalvan. Marshal Haggard sends you to find Tavernkeep Smitts, who may know the hand behind a page from Stalvan's journal. Marshal Haggard cannot read the faded writing on the torn journal page you recovered from his chest in Elwynn Forest. His failing eyesight leaves the words beyond him. He recalls serving with the Stormwind Guard and spending evenings at the Scarlet Raven Tavern in Darkshire. So he sends you across the river to Tavernkeep Smitts, whose years behind the bar have made him a keeper of local history and rumors.

quest:78124.text: Nar'thalas Almanac. Scholars seek the Nar'thalas Almanac to preserve ancient magical study. Its recovery brings forgotten lore into a library where researchers can study it. A rare work of arcane study, the Nar'thalas Almanac comes from the ancient traditions of pre-Sundering night elven scholarship. For caretakers of great archives, securing the volume rescues centuries-old lore from obscurity and adds an important piece of history to their shelves. Those who uncover neglected works help bridge forgotten antiquity and modern scholarship. Across Azeroth, archivists and researchers seek lost treatises, field notes, and chronicles. Bringing the Nar'thalas Almanac to a dedicated library lets its keepers safeguard, catalog, and study it, rather than leave it to rot in ruins or fall into careless hands. Each recovered volume offers fresh insight into the arcane arts of past eras.

quest:78143.text: Secrets of the Dreamers. A library's scholars seek writings tied to the Dreamers and other magical lore. Travelers bring forgotten works from across the realm, where they can be studied and kept in the archives. Scholars across the realm depend on travelers to recover rare magical texts and historical treatises. These works lie in ancient ruins or private hoards, far from the archives. So adventurers carry them safely to those who study Azeroth's arcane mysteries and preserve its lore. When travelers bring in treatises, archivists add them to the library's permanent collection. Researchers seek obscure writings on the Emerald Dream and arcane theory. Their work continues, and they welcome further magical texts found in the field.

quest:79.text:
The Legend of Stalvan. In Darkshire, The Legend of Stalvan rests on muddy pages and new proof. Tavernkeep Smitts gives you the pages and sends you to Commander Althea Ebonlocke. Tavernkeep Smitts and Marshal Haggard once investigated the slaughter of a visiting noble family in Duskwood. Haggard then led the Stormwind Guard. At the scene, they found torn, muddy journal pages, but had no handwriting samples or other papers to confirm who wrote them. So the notes could not formally implicate the recluse rumored to live in the wilderness.

Now evidence gathered across Elwynn, Westfall, and Duskwood links the handwriting to Stalvan Mistmantle. The old rumors have become proof of murder.

quest:79007.text: ... and that note you found. At a recent campsite, cooling embers and scattered supplies are all that remain. A scorched parchment bears a riddle about finding a twin land, the only clue left behind. A recent campfire is dying beside scattered provisions and a blistered piece of paper. Whoever stayed here left recently, and the parchment narrowly escaped the flames. The supplies remain exposed, as though the traveler departed in haste or was interrupted. The surviving scrap bears one instruction: “Not all that burns is lost. Find the twin land, find the place.” No signature, coordinates, or further context survived the fire. The riddle is the only trail left for whoever finds it.

quest:79008.text: ... and that note you found. A scorched note lies beside a dying campfire in Westfall. Its brief message points to a place called the twin land. Travelers crossing Westfall’s abandoned fields and wind-scoured plains find camps left by vagrants, outlaws, or desperate wanderers. This small camp was left in haste or secrecy. Its provisions lie abandoned, embers still glow, and a scorched slip of parchment rests among the scattered debris. The blistered note bears two short sentences: “Not all that burns is lost. Find the twin land, find the place.” Its words point away from Westfall but give no clear direction. What place shares a name, geography, or fate with this land?

quest:79091.text: Archmage Antonidas: The Unabridged Autobiography. In Ironforge, you seek Archmage Antonidas: The Unabridged Autobiography. The rare volume holds the late Kirin Tor leader's own account and offers insight into Dalaran's history and high arcane scholarship. Archmage Antonidas led the Kirin Tor for decades and ruled Dalaran. One of Azeroth's most brilliant minds, he rose through the ranks of the Violet Citadel and mastered the arcane. His unabridged autobiography records his leadership during the Second and Third Wars. For scholars and practitioners of magic, it offers a firsthand view of Dalaran's inner workings and the arcane arts. Before reaching its new home, the rare manuscript rested in Ironforge's grand library. In the Hall of Explorers, dwarven archivists kept it beside ancient titan relics and dwarven histories. Their vast collections hold texts gathered from ruins and foreign kingdoms across Azeroth. Yet arcane scholars elsewhere seek such works for their own collections, sure the busy archivists will never notice one missing volume.

quest:79092.text:
Archmage Theocritus' Research Journal. At the Tower of Azora, Archmage Theocritus keeps a journal of his investigations. Now you carry its magical insights to the scholars of the Ironforge Library, where they can join the dwarven archive. Archmage Theocritus is an esteemed spellcaster known throughout the Alliance. He is stationed at the Tower of Azora in eastern Elwynn Forest, where he has studied alone for years. His investigations range from curious artifacts and ley line anomalies to nearby magical threats.

He records his findings in detailed journals. This volume offers a rare chance to study the personal observations of a senior Kirin Tor archmage. The Explorers' League and the caretakers of the Ironforge Library maintain one of the continent's greatest archives. You bring Archmage Theocritus' Research Journal to them, helping preserve and catalog its arcane insights beside the historic volumes of Khaz Modan. The librarians welcome further magical discoveries that can broaden their shared wisdom.

quest:79093.text: Rumi of Gnomeregan: The Collected Works. A compiled work by Rumi of Gnomeregan is sought for a library’s collection. Its pages preserve gnomish writings and knowledge that might otherwise be lost. Gnomish writings were scattered, buried, or left in danger when troggs overran Gnomeregan. Now scholars and archivists seek surviving manuscripts, treatises, and compiled works. They hope to keep the wisdom and ingenuity of gnomish thinkers alive. When travelers find collected works in the field and bring them to the archives, curators add them to their growing collections. Each recovered manuscript widens what scholars can study. Archivists welcome more magical and historical texts, keeping them within reach of scholars, mages, and historians who guard Azeroth’s learning.

quest:79095.text: The Apothecary's Metaphysical Primer. Curators seek The Apothecary's Metaphysical Primer to enrich their archives. Its delivery helps preserve rare alchemical and arcane theory for researchers and spellcasters. Curators welcome The Apothecary's Metaphysical Primer for its study of esoteric and magical principles. Owen Thadd adds the text directly to his working collection of magical references. Owen Thadd's collection in Undercity preserves specialized treatises. By bringing him rare primers on arcane and alchemical theory, you help keep metaphysical insights safe in the archives and accessible to researchers instead of leaving them lost in the wilderness.

quest:79097.text: Baxtan: On Destructive Magics. At the library, Baxtan: On Destructive Magics joins the works scholars gather to understand dangerous arcane power. Scholars seek to preserve what is known of arcane lore. When you find a text on destructive magic, its place is in careful academic keeping. There, its power and peril can be understood instead of lost. The library holds works on history, science, and the arcane.
